# Fixture book run, paged-flat

Generated by `scripts/bench_driver.py` from raw records that are not committed. Do not edit by hand.

Host: **macOS (M4 Max)**. Numbers from the two hosts are never mixed.

**macOS (M4 Max) is not a pinned host.** macOS offers no way to pin a thread, so each process ran wherever the scheduler put it, beside whatever else the machine was doing under `measure.sh`'s lock. Every figure here is a macOS figure, and a bar set on x86 Linux is not passed or failed by one.

## Summary

Each repetition is a fresh process: one warm-up pass, excluded from every figure here, then a throughput pass and a separate latency pass, each on a fresh book, and a second process for the untimed pass of counters and memory. Every design of the run ran in each repetition, one after the other. 3 repetitions.

The mean service time is the throughput pass's time over every message, frame walk included (T-LAT-3). The batch mean is the same time over the 3,312 book messages, carteret's denominator: `A`, `F`, `E`, `C`, `X`, `D`, `U`, `P` and `Q` (T-LAT-4).

## How this run reads the day

The day was mapped read-only, and each pass reads the mapping in place. After each message the book applied, the best bid and ask on its locate, price and shares, were read and compared with the last seen there: inside the throughput pass's time, outside each latency span. This is itch-book's T-BOOK-2 method, `itch-replay --book`: it maps the file and checks the best bid and ask, price and shares, after every book event.

## Book memory

T-BOOK-3. Read from phys_footprint from task_info(TASK_VM_INFO), in a process of its own that builds no other book first: once before the book is built, once after, every 1,048,576 messages of the untimed pass and at its end. The book's memory is the most charged at any reading less the reading before it was built. That is what the book itself takes, not the mapped file or the input copy, which are in the first reading, and not the latency samples, which that process never makes. itch-book's figure is peak RSS less the input buffer, the same quantity read another way.

| Figure | Median | Min | Max | CV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
